name: Keele STarT Back Screening Tool

citations.text: Hill JC, Dunn KM, Lewis M, et al. A primary care back pain screening tool: identifying patient subgroups for initial treatment. Arthritis Rheum. 2008;59(5):632-641.

validated_population: Adults with low back pain in primary care. Self-administered.
license_note: © Keele University. Free to use for clinical care; wording must not be changed; commercial use requires a license from Keele University. Verify terms at keele.ac.uk/sbst before deployment.

red_flags.question: Do you have numbness around the groin or buttocks, or new trouble controlling your bladder or bowels?
red_flags.help: These can be signs of pressure on the nerves at the base of the spine (cauda equina), which is an emergency.

red_flags.question: Do you have new weakness in a leg, or a foot that drags or slaps when you walk?
red_flags.help: New weakness can mean nerve compression.

red_flags.question: With this back pain, do you have a fever, a history of cancer, recent unexplained weight loss, or injected drug use?
red_flags.help: These increase the chance of a serious cause.

items.question: Do you agree or disagree: "My back pain has spread down my leg(s) at some time in the last 2 weeks"
items.help: Pain that travels below the buttock.

items.question: Do you agree or disagree: "I have had pain in the shoulder or neck at some time in the last 2 weeks"
Do you agree or disagree: "I have only walked short distances because of my back pain"
Do you agree or disagree: "In the last 2 weeks, I have dressed more slowly than usual because of back pain"
Do you agree or disagree: "It's not really safe for a person with a condition like mine to be physically active"
Do you agree or disagree: "Worrying thoughts have been going through my mind a lot of the time"
Do you agree or disagree: "I feel that my back pain is terrible and it's never going to get any better"
items.help: Your own view of the pain.

items.question: Do you agree or disagree: "In general I have not enjoyed all the things I used to enjoy"
Overall, how bothersome has your back pain been in the last 2 weeks?

scoring.threshold_text: Total 0–3 = low risk. Total 4 or more: psychosocial subscale (Q5–Q9) 0–3 = medium risk; 4–5 = high risk.

low.label: Low risk of long-term back problems
low.interpretation: Your answers suggest a low risk of long-term disability from back pain. Most people in this group improve with self-care.
low.recommendation: Stay active and manage pain at home.

care.within: Self-care; primary care if not improving in 4 to 6 weeks
care.where_detail: Home care. Book a primary care visit if pain is not improving after 4 to 6 weeks.
ed_redirect: Numbness in groin/buttocks or loss of bladder or bowel control
self_care: Heat and over-the-counter pain relievers as labeled.

medium.label: Medium risk of long-term back problems
medium.interpretation: Your answers suggest a medium risk. In the STarT Back trial, this group did better with physical therapy.
medium.recommendation: Book a physical therapy or primary care visit.

care.where_detail: Physical therapist (most U.S. states allow direct access without a referral) or primary care.
ed_redirect: Numbness in groin/buttocks or loss of bladder or bowel control

high.label: High risk of long-term back problems
high.interpretation: Your answers suggest a high risk, often with worry or low mood linked to the pain. This group did better with physical therapy that also addresses thoughts and feelings about pain.
high.recommendation: Book a primary care visit to arrange combined physical and psychological care.

care.where_detail: Primary care clinic, or a physical therapist trained in psychologically informed care.
ed_redirect: Numbness in groin/buttocks or loss of bladder or bowel control
